# Private-lane markers — one extended-regex per line, matched case-insensitively
# against every tracked text file by .github/workflows/private-marker-guard.yml.
#
# Each pattern earned its place: on 2026-07-28 an audit found material in the
# PUBLIC tree that the previous guard (literal "(PRIVATE)" + `^AGENT-`) could
# not see. The comment above each group names what it would have caught.
#
# Add `guard-allow` on a line to exempt a deliberate mention.

# --- DIRECTIVE: the file itself says it must not be published -----------------
# caught: intel-1984.md "(for the record; do NOT post)";
#         WATCHLIST.md "UNCOMMITTED, private-fork only until reviewed";
#         RESULTS-flagship-scale671.md "DRAFT — held for owner review; not
#         stamped, not committed" (and it was committed).
do NOT post
must not reach the public remote
private-fork only
private fork only
not stamped, not committed
held for owner review
uncommitted, private
moves to the public repo at the gate

# --- LANE: names the private sibling, its branches, or its lineage ------------
# caught: "Code: private fork `mxfp4_pack_ref/...`", "(private-lineage)",
#         "e4b control @ e62a7a0 (`private`)", private branch names.
\(PRIVATE\)
private fork
private-lineage
private-only
e4b-ssdtier
grouped-nf4-gemm-private
experts4bit-qlora-private

# --- HOSTPATH: evidence that only exists on the author's machines -------------
# caught: "~/e4b-evidence/routed-residual/", "~/e4b-outbox/...-DRAFT.md".
~/e4b-outbox
~/e4b-evidence
~/gnf4-lat
~/\.runpod

# --- OPSEC: engagement choreography aimed at third-party projects -------------
# caught: ops-log.md "Two-Comment Coordination Operation", "radio silence
#         resumes", "aftermath rails armed". Reads as manipulation of an
#         upstream project regardless of intent.
radio silence
aftermath rails
coordination operation
do not solicit
not to be solicited

# --- DOSSIER: strategic assessment of a named individual ----------------------
# caught: intel-1984.md treating a contributor's published error figures as
#         "candidate FLEET contributions ... usable only once he appears on".
# Keep this narrow: it targets the framing, not ordinary attribution.
intel notes —
candidate FLEET contribution
FLEET contributions

# --- INFRA: home-network and rented-host identifiers --------------------------
# caught: "QNAP TVS-h1688X", the UPS model plus a note about which service was
#         NOT listening; RunPod pod ids in receipts; lab IPs.
TVS-h1688X
PhxTec
10\.0\.0\.[0-9]{1,3}
192\.168\.[0-9]{1,3}\.[0-9]{1,3}

# --- e4b PRIVATE LANE ---------------------------------------------------------
# This repo has a private sibling (experts4bit-qlora-private) holding the
# commercial lean-prefill engine and the routed-staging work. These branch names
# and the integration branch must never appear in the public tree: naming them
# discloses the private topology even when no code leaks.
feat/pipelined-lean-prefill
perf/routed-staging-overhead
integration/lean-onto-routed-staging
# --- control-plane markers (added with the 2026-09-06 boundary directive) ---
# The organisational record — Slack coordination, seats, the control-plane and
# corpus repositories — is private. These patterns are what the guard could not
# see before: a Slack permalink validator, a workspace channel id, the private
# repository URLs and the runtime's own dot-directory all reached this tree
# through files the old list had no expression for.
cerin-amroth\.slack\.com
C0BV5028SGM
pjordanandrsn/adertha-
pjordanandrsn/org-corpus
\.adertha/
# adertha:// URIs name artifacts in the private store; one reached a tracked file (2026-10-10).
adertha://

# --- ADDED-ONLY: checked on the lines a change ADDS, never on the merged tree --------------
# A PR reference into the private control-plane repo ("<repo>#N") reached 73 lines of merged
# public files before the guard knew the form (2026-10-19). History keeps them: registrations
# and sealed records are not rewritten after the fact. New lines may not add one. The workflow
# diffs a change against its merge base; the pre-push hook diffs a push against the remote tip.
# Format: "#added-only: REGEX" (extended, case-insensitive); each needs a canary line.
#added-only: adertha(-agents)?#[0-9]

# The private receipt store's checkout name and branch, and absolute home-directory paths, follow the same rule:
# a public record names "the private receipt store" and the run id, with paths relative to the run; merged records keep theirs.
#added-only: adertha-receipts
#added-only: cdo/state-
#added-only: /Users/[a-z][a-z0-9._-]*/
# Any /home/<name>/ except /home/node/, a container home that many records name legitimately:
#added-only: /home/(n|no|nod|[^n/][^/]*|n[^o/][^/]*|no[^d/][^/]*|nod[^e/][^/]*|node[^/]+)/

# The control plane's bare name (2026-10-23): it reached public comments as a module path and as "the <name>
# reconciler", and no rule above sees the bare word. Public text says what the tool does instead: "the launcher",
# "the launcher's host probe", "the receipt store", "the message bus", "the control plane". The lines already
# merged keep theirs: many sit in closed kits whose files are pinned by sha256. No trailing word boundary: "_" is a
# word character, so one would let identifiers (a module file, an UPPER_CASE environment variable) through.
#added-only: \badertha

# A rented card's GPU UUID (nvidia-smi's uuid; 2026-10-24): it identifies one physical device, and a public receipt
# never needs it. Receipt files that carry one (forensics.txt, outer.log, a trainer's device record) are store-only
# (STORE-ONLY.sha256), or a public projection of only the fields a reducer reads. Files merged before the rule keep
# theirs; new lines may not add one.
#added-only: GPU-[0-9a-f]{8}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{12}

# --- RECEIPT STORE: the private receipt store's ledger and receipt records ----
# The store's records are private, and none of the patterns above can see them.
# They are matched by SHAPE, never by name: this file is public, so naming the
# store or any private repository here would publish it.
Append-only ledger: one JSON object per line
"external_receipt"[[:space:]]*:
# A ledger row is a line carrying all four keys, in any order. An "#all-of:" line
# lists ERE terms, separated by single spaces, that must ALL match the same line
# (git grep --and). Every other reader of this file skips it as a comment.
#all-of: "run_id"[[:space:]]*: "date_utc"[[:space:]]*: "role"[[:space:]]*: "cost_usd"[[:space:]]*:
# Fixture exemptions. A path named by an "#exempt-fixture:" line is skipped by
# every scan only while it holds at most MAX-LINES lines AND its sha256 equals
# the pin (scripts/guard_fixture_pin.sh); otherwise the guard fails. Format:
# "#exempt-fixture: PATH MAX-LINES SHA256". The two below are the ledger header
# and one $0 row, which the DQ11 census tests parse; the third is census-7's one stalled row (#1083).
#exempt-fixture: tests/fixtures/dq11-census-refused/canonical-ledger.jsonl 2 4030f01c74fb263e665c900d8d9f04ef89ee224c74429d62c4ffdd36b11569d2
#exempt-fixture: tests/fixtures/dq11-census-refused/ledger.jsonl 1 c106ef976fbc5fa7a57d09864d97dfd7a502b3fb034860e502f11080f06a2d66
#exempt-fixture: tests/fixtures/dq11-census-stalled/ledger.jsonl 1 8b0954615b702828914563eb795b9ecacb303316a2ffeed033998eb82c7b83d9
